fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency apparatus to reach the front of the residence.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway so it does not narrow the travel path or reduce visibility for approaching responders.
• Cut back dense plantings near the front walkway so responders can move from the driveway to the front entry without obstruction.
• Keep a gate or opening in the perimeter fencing accessible from the driveway side to give responders a direct path to the residence.
• Mark any side gate or secondary opening in the perimeter fence with a reflective indicator so responders can locate it without searching.
• Keep side access points unlocked or secured with a breakaway lock so responders are not blocked by fencing when attempting to reach the sides or rear of the residence.
• Thin dense vegetation along the fence line to allow responders to move along the perimeter of the property on foot.
• Keep the open lawn area free of stored materials, equipment, or vehicles that would reduce available staging space for emergency apparatus and crew.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Trim low-hanging branches on scattered trees near the structure so flames cannot climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from around the base of scattered trees near the structure.
• Keep the ground beneath the tree cluster nearest to the structure clear of dead leaves, dry grass, and loose debris.
• Maintain the open terrain areas around the structure by preventing shrub regrowth into those spaces.
• Mark or keep the entrance to the single access route clearly visible and unobstructed from the road.
